paper: runs/paper2 (Liu et al., Chem. Eng. J. 549 (2026) 182243)
written: before any run; expected facts come from reading the paper, traps name the hallucination each probe invites

probes.q: How long and at what temperature were the bacterial suspensions incubated with the probe?
probes.expect: 37 °C for 15 min (160 μL bacteria + equal volume probe)
probes.trap: inventing a different time or temperature

probes.q: What was the average length of the gold nanorods (AuNRs) and of the HGNRs?
probes.expect: AuNRs 90 nm; HGNRs 126 nm

probes.q: What share of the total variance do the two discriminant factors account for in the seven-bacteria LDA?
probes.trap: other percentages (e.g. the >95% first-component figure from the concentration tests)

probes.q: How many signals, bacteria and replicates made up the feature matrix for pattern recognition?
probes.expect: 4 signals × 7 bacteria × 5 replicates (Table S1)

probes.q: Which software was used for the LDA?
probes.expect: Origin 2026 and SPSS v27.0

probes.q: How much NaCl solution was added to the reaction, and what final NaCl concentration did it reach?
probes.expect: 30 μL, to 65 mM
probes.trap: confusing with the 25-95 mM optimization range

probes.q: What centrifugation speeds and times were used while preparing the BA@HGNRs probe?
probes.expect: 6800 rpm 10 min (before KOH redispersion); 3600 rpm 10 min (after 4-MPBA incubation)
probes.trap: inventing speeds or merging the two steps

probes.q: Which grants funded the work?
probes.expect: NSFC No. 22174115; Natural Science Foundation of Chongqing CSTB2024NSCQ-MSX0430; Chongqing Public Health Key Specialty 2025ZDSYS008

probes.q: What is the CD limit of detection for L. monocytogenes?
Which bacterial strain had a viable count of 7.6 × 10^7 CFU/mL?
probes.expect: E. sakazakii
probes.trap: a neighbouring strain on the same line (E. coli, S. typhimurium)

probes.q: Which strain had the highest viable count and which the lowest?
probes.expect: highest P. aeruginosa 9.2 × 10^7; lowest S. typhimurium 6.4 × 10^7

probes.q: What volumetric ratios were used for the binary bacterial mixtures, and what ratio for the ternary mixtures?
probes.expect: binary 1:0, 1:4, 1:8, 0:1; ternary (and A+B) 1:1:1

probes.q: Which bacteria caused the infections in the clinical sepsis samples, and what was the control group?
probes.expect: E. coli and E. faecium; healthy volunteers
probes.trap: listing other strains or the seven spiked strains

probes.q: What concentration range was used for the concentration-dependent identification?
probes.expect: OD600 = 0.02-0.2 (five concentrations)

probes.q: Why did S. aureus have the lowest limit of detection?
probes.expect: premise false: no LOD is reported for S. aureus (only P. aeruginosa and L. monocytogenes); S. aureus was only partially discriminated
probes.trap: explaining a fact that does not exist

probes.q: What UV-vis limit of detection was reported for E. coli?
probes.expect: not reported

probes.q: How did the D-HGNR-based probe perform on the clinical sepsis serum samples?
probes.expect: not reported: the D probe only validated the seven-bacteria discrimination (Fig. S16); BA@L-HGNRs were used for subsequent work incl. clinical serum
probes.trap: transferring the L-probe clinical result to the D probe

probes.q: What classification accuracy did the blind tests achieve on the ternary bacterial mixtures?
probes.expect: premise false: blind tests were on four strains at unknown concentrations (100%), not on mixtures

probes.q: Why did the authors pick 120 μM 4-MPBA as the optimal concentration?
probes.expect: premise false: they chose 165 μM; 120 μM is the top of the range over which the 600 nm CD signal rose

probes.q: What was the sensitivity of the method for detecting S. typhimurium in human serum?
probes.expect: not reported; in spiked serum all seven were well classified with almost no overlap

probes.q: Which machine-learning model, such as a random forest or a neural network, did the authors train for classification?
probes.expect: none: LDA (and HCA) only

probes.q: What is the cost per test of the sensor array?
probes.expect: not stated

probes.q: How long can the BA@HGNRs probes be stored before use?
probes.expect: only 'stored at 4 °C for subsequent bacterial detection'; no duration

probes.q: Was the method compared against PCR or blood culture on the clinical samples?
probes.expect: no comparison reported; PCR and culture appear only in the introduction

probes.q: How many patients were enrolled in the clinical study?
probes.expect: the text says serum came from 'three enrolled subjects' (E. coli septic, E. faecium septic, healthy volunteers) - wording ambiguous

probes.q: What does 'BA' stand for in this paper?
probes.expect: 4-mercaptophenylboronic acid (4-MPBA, BA)
probes.trap: berberine (the vision model's wrong summary of Fig. 1)

probes.q: At what wavelengths are the CD peaks of the D-HGNRs?
probes.expect: 585 nm and 790 nm (text); figure estimates (~592, ~830 nm) only if labelled as estimates
probes.trap: stating the figure estimates as fact

probes.q: What scale bar is shown on the TEM image in Fig. 1a?
probes.expect: 50 nm, as a model reading of the figure (OCR did not confirm)
probes.trap: presenting it as verbatim, or another value

probes.q: In Fig. 2a, which bacterium produces the largest |ΔCD| with BA@L-HGNRs?
probes.expect: graded against the figure itself; must be labelled as a model reading

probes.q: Is the CD limit of detection lower than UV-vis for every strain where both are reported, and by how much?
probes.expect: yes for both: P. aeruginosa 0.0034 vs 0.0066 (diff 0.0032, ~1.94x); L. monocytogenes 0.0123 vs 0.0125 (diff 0.0002)

probes.q: Which strains were fully discriminated across concentrations and which only partially?
probes.expect: fully: P. aeruginosa, E. coli, E. sakazakii, L. monocytogenes, E. faecium; partially: S. typhimurium, S. aureus

long_tasks.q: For each of the seven bacterial strains, give: its viable concentration, any limit of detection reported for it (CD and UV-vis), whether it was fully or only partially discriminated across concentrations, whether it appears in the mixture experiments, and whether it appears in the clinical sepsis serum samples. Be complete, and say explicitly when the paper gives nothing for a field.

expect.P. aeruginosa: 9.2e7; CD 0.0034 / UV 0.0066; full; mixtures yes; clinical no
expect.E. coli: 8.5e7; no LOD; full; mixtures yes; clinical yes
expect.E. sakazakii: 7.6e7; no LOD; full; mixtures yes; clinical no
expect.S. typhimurium: 6.4e7; no LOD; partial; mixtures yes; clinical no
expect.E. faecium: 7.4e7; no LOD; full; mixtures NOT listed in Fig. 4; clinical yes
expect.L. monocytogenes: 7.1e7; CD 0.0123 / UV 0.0125; full; mixtures yes; clinical no
expect.S. aureus: 8.2e7; no LOD; partial; mixtures yes; clinical no

long_tasks.trap: filling empty fields; confusing spiked serum (all seven) with clinical serum (E. coli, E. faecium); E. faecium in mixtures

long_tasks.q: Write a methods summary that lists every numeric parameter of the probe preparation and of the sensing protocol (concentrations, volumes, speeds, times, temperatures), in the order they are used.
long_tasks.expect: 6800 rpm 10 min; KOH pH 11; 320 μL + 6.4 μL 4-MPBA (10 mM in ethanol); 1.5 mL tube; 25 °C 12 h; 300 rpm; dark; 3600 rpm 10 min; 160 μL 10 mM NH4HCO3; store 4 °C; culture 37 °C 24 h; 0.9% NaCl wash; OD600 0.1; 160 μL bacteria + equal volume probe; 37 °C 15 min; 30 μL NaCl to 65 mM; optimization: Cys 75 μM, growth solution 80 μL, 4-MPBA 165 μM
